turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just cannot seem to keep my work in order anymore. I work at a dry cleaner's, you see. It's usually fine, but lately... well, my sister says I've always been a bit messy, but she's one to talk. She left her purse at the grocery store twice last month. She buys those really expensive leather ones, too, the kind with the heavy buckles. 

But anyway, at the shop, I've got tickets, receipts, workshop notes, and the actual customer jobs all just piled together. It's a complete disaster. Just yesterday this man came in looking for his wife's silk blouse, the one with the pearl buttons? Beautiful blouse, really, I think she got it at that boutique downtown. But I couldn't find his ticket because everything is just in these huge stacks everywhere. I look at the counter and I just do not know what to handle first. I think I spent twenty minutes just moving hangers from one rack to another before I even started on the till. 

Wait, what was the question again? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, the piles. It's just getting to be too much.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient explicitly states they cannot keep their work in order, have piles of mixed items, and do not know what to handle first.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient describes being unable to find a customer's ticket because it was lost in huge stacks of items.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by unrelated thoughts (their sister's purse, the details of a customer's blouse) and forgets the doctor's initial question.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned your sister says you've always been a bit messy. How long have you been having this trouble keeping things organized at work — is this something new that's been happening recently, or has it always been this way?
turns.patient_response:
Well, she's right about the messy part, I guess. I mean, my bedroom growing up was always a disaster zone. My mother used to say I was building a nest out of dirty laundry and old magazines. She read a lot of magazines, my mom did—mostly those home and garden ones, even though we lived in an apartment and didn't have a garden. She tried growing tomatoes on the fire escape once, but the pigeons kept getting to them. 

But as far as work goes... the real trouble, I mean the kind where I'm actually losing things and getting overwhelmed by the piles, that's been going on for about two years and two months. That's when I started trying to change the business into this more complicated boutique model. You know, offering specialized care for delicate fabrics, hand-pressing, that sort of thing. I thought it would bring in a better clientele. And it did! We started getting people from the nice neighborhoods over by the park. There's this one lady who brings in these incredible vintage dresses. She told me she goes to estate sales every weekend. I went to an estate sale once, but it just felt so sad, looking at all of someone's old teacups and things. I ended up buying a lamp I didn't even need. 

But yeah, since I made that switch at the shop a couple of years ago, it's just been too much to keep track of.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes their childhood bedroom as a 'disaster zone' and mentions getting overwhelmed by piles and having 'too much to keep track of' at work.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient explicitly states they are 'actually losing things' at work.

turns.doctor_question: When you're trying to organize things at work or handle tasks, do you find your mind wandering or jumping from one thing to another, or is it more that you just have too much stuff to manage?

It was this itchy, awful thing my aunt knit for me, and I wore it to choir practice once. Oh, I sing in the church choir, by the way. We're actually trying to plan our Christmas program right now, which is a whole other headache because the soprano section wants to do all these complicated arrangements, and I'm just an alto, so I just want to stick to the traditional carols. 

Anyway, I'll be thinking about the choir plans, or maybe wondering if I left the stove on at home—I made oatmeal this morning, the steel-cut kind that takes forever to cook—and then suddenly twenty minutes have gone by. I'll look back down at the counter and realize I missed half of what I was supposed to check on the orders. So yeah, I just drift off into my own world, I guess.

I had this one folder, it was bright red with little yellow stars on it—my mom bought it for me at Woolworth's. Remember Woolworth's? I loved that store. They had a lunch counter where you could get a grilled cheese sandwich and a cherry Coke. The cherry Coke always had that real maraschino cherry at the bottom, and I'd save it for the very last bite. I tried making those at home once for my niece's birthday party, but I bought the wrong kind of syrup and it just tasted like cough medicine. The kids wouldn't touch it. We ended up just having lemonade, which was fine, but I was so disappointed about the cherry Cokes. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, school. Yeah, I'd lose my papers even with that red star folder, and the teachers always had to remind me to actually finish my work. I'd start a worksheet and just... drift off.
